newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes firmer despite rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes firmer despite rate cut.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev firmed to 978-980 per mark at the close from the opening's 980-983 due to larger foreign currency supply, coming mainly from final clients and despite the rate cut, dealers said.
* The lev closed at 1,689-1,692 per dollar, up from the morning's 1,692-1,696, tracking the mark-dollar cross on international markets, dealers said.

* Final clients were selling foreign currency for levs to meet pending payments, while demand was low despite the falling yield on government securities and the cut in the main interest rate ahead of the lev peg at 1,000 per mark under a currency board.
* The Bulgarian National Bank cut on Friday its main interest rate to a effective annual on monthly basis 16.30 percent, from 42.24 percent now.
* The average yield to maturity on the paper fell to 0.58 percent at today's auction from 0.62 percent on Thursday, 0.69 percent on Wednesday and 0.72 percent on Tuesday.
